questions.text: Which of the following areas is listed as a DANGER AREA under RA 7279 (Urban Development and Housing Act), Section 28, where eviction may be lawful?

options.text: Esteros, railroad tracks, garbage dumps, riverbanks, shorelines, waterways, and other public places where occupation poses danger to life and property.
Any private residential subdivision built before 1992, regardless of physical hazard.
Any land within 50 kilometers of an active fault line, with no other condition.
Any land owned by a government-owned or controlled corporation, regardless of hazard.

rationale.a: Correct. RA 7279 Section 28 lists danger areas by type: esteros, railroad tracks, garbage dumps, riverbanks, shorelines, waterways, and other public places where the occupation poses danger to life and property. The statute does not specify a numeric setback; specific distances come from other codes (e.g., PD 1067 easements).
rationale.b: Wrong. RA 7279 does not classify all pre-1992 subdivisions as danger areas.
rationale.c: Wrong. RA 7279 does not impose a 50-kilometer fault-line buffer. Fault setbacks come from PHIVOLCS guidance (5-meter minimum) and CLUP integration, not from RA 7279.
rationale.d: Wrong. Government ownership alone does not make land a danger area under RA 7279; the listed physical hazards do.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 Section 28 enumerates danger areas by physical type. Numeric setback distances are not in RA 7279 itself; they come from related codes such as PD 1067. Section 28 safeguards and Section 29 relocation still apply even in danger-area evictions.
rationale.takeaway: Do not attach a '3-meter' figure to RA 7279 danger areas. RA 7279 lists danger areas by type; numeric easements come from PD 1067 (Water Code) and other codes.

questions.text: Under RA 10884 (Balanced Housing Development Program, 2016), which amended Section 18 of RA 7279, what socialized-housing allocation applies to a SUBDIVISION project?

options.text: At least 5 percent of total subdivision area or project cost, at the developer's option
At least 15 percent of total subdivision area or project cost, at the developer's option
At least 20 percent of total subdivision area or project cost, at the developer's option
At least 30 percent of total subdivision area or project cost, at the developer's option

rationale.a: Wrong. 5% applies to CONDOMINIUM projects under RA 10884, not subdivisions.
rationale.b: Correct. RA 10884 Section 2(b) reduced the subdivision (horizontal) requirement from the original RA 7279 figure of 20% to at least 15% of total subdivision area or project cost at the developer's option.
rationale.c: Wrong. 20% was the original RA 7279 (1992) requirement; RA 10884 (2016) reduced it to 15% for subdivisions.
rationale.d: Wrong. 30% is the PD 1216 / PD 957 non-buildable open-space requirement for subdivisions of 1 hectare or more, not a balanced-housing figure.
rationale.correct: RA 10884 (2016), Section 2(b) amending RA 7279 Section 18, requires owners/developers of subdivision projects to develop an area for socialized housing equivalent to at least 15 percent of the total subdivision area or project cost, at the option of the developer. For condominium projects the figure is 5%.
rationale.takeaway: RA 10884 reduced the subdivision balanced-housing share from RA 7279's 20% to 15% (and set condominiums at 5%). The figure is fixed at 15% for subdivisions, not '15-20%'.

questions.text: An informal settler community occupies the banks of an estero, an area listed as a danger area under RA 7279. The LGU initiates eviction. Which statement correctly describes the procedural requirements?

options.text: Eviction may proceed immediately without notice because the area is a danger zone.
Notice and other Section 28 safeguards may be waived because the area is a danger zone.

Danger-area listing permits eviction, but RA 7279 Section 28 safeguards (including at least 30-day notice, consultation on resettlement, presence of LGU officials) and Section 29 relocation duties still apply.
Danger-area occupants lose all RA 7279 rights and must self-relocate at their own expense.

rationale.a: Wrong. Even danger-area evictions require notice and the other Section 28 safeguards.
rationale.b: Wrong. The Section 28 safeguards are not waived by danger-area status. Notice, consultation, presence of officials, and adequate relocation remain mandatory.
rationale.c: Correct. RA 7279 Section 28 lists occupancy of danger areas as one of the lawful grounds for eviction, but the same section prescribes procedural safeguards (at least 30 days notice, consultation on resettlement, presence of LGU officials, proper identification, regular hours/good weather, limits on heavy equipment, proper police uniforms, and adequate relocation). Section 29 obliges LGUs, with the NHA, to provide relocation sites with basic services and livelihood access.
rationale.d: Wrong. RA 7279 does not strip danger-area occupants of all rights; relocation duty rests on the LGU and NHA, not on the occupants.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 Section 28 + Section 29: danger-area status permits eviction but does NOT waive the procedural safeguards or the government's relocation obligation.
rationale.takeaway: Do not waive notice or resettlement for danger-area occupants. The RA 7279 framework requires safeguards plus LGU/NHA relocation in all evictions of underprivileged and homeless citizens.
